subject: Urgent: sustained request timeouts and throughput depletion — Finly reserved pool
messages:
From: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@finly.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.example
Cc: ops@finly.com
Date: 2026-12-02T08:14:00Z
Subject: Production timeouts — reserved pool underperforming

Sean —

We started seeing elevated 504s and a sharp drop in completed requests against our reserved pool at ~07:40 PT this morning. Impacting transaction enrichment jobs and the user-facing approval flow. Error rate climbed from <0.1% to ~6% and median latency slipped from 120ms to >900ms.

We rely on the reserved throughput contract — this is blocking our peak morning window. Can you confirm whether this is a customer-side issue (our traffic) or a Redwood capacity problem? We opened an incident ticket (attached logs) but need an immediate mitigation plan.

Tom
Director, Platform
Finly

Attachments: request_logs_20261202.zip, slo-snapshot-20261202.png

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.example
To: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@finly.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-12-02T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — reserved pool underperforming

Tom — thanks for the data and the quick heads-up. I'm escalating this immediately.

Quick notes:
- I've looped in Laura (CSM) and Neha (SRE) to triage and confirm whether reserved capacity is returning degraded throughput.
- Can you confirm if any bursty job runs started at 07:30-08:00 PT beyond your typical pattern? That helps us rule out traffic anomalies.

Next steps from our side by EOD: 1) initial root cause triage and SLO snapshot; 2) temporary routing options (hosted fallback or capacity burst) to reduce customer-visible errors; 3) plan for permanent remediation if this is tied to pool saturation.

I'll keep you posted every 30–45 minutes while we investigate.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Cc: tom.mercer@finly.com
Date: 2026-12-02T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — reserved pool underperforming

Summary of initial findings (09:00 PT):
- Metrics: sustained queue growth on pool rsv-prod-us-west-2-19 starting 07:35 UTC-8; 95th pct latency correlates with batch assembly timeouts and increased preemption events on a subset of GPUs.
- Logs: kernel eviction spikes and memory pressure on two nodes; we see elevated retry rates from the customer's RL worker process.
- No config changes detected on Finly side in the provided interval.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Activate emergency burst (15% extra capacity) for Finly's pool for 2 hours while we drain the backlog. Requires exec approval for overcommit charge and network routing change.
2) Failover a fraction (~20%) of production traffic to a compatible hosted variant (same model family, slightly lower quantization) — minimal code change on your side; expected transient quality delta.
3) Apply temporary request-rate throttle on non-critical endpoints (requires Finly sign-off).

I've attached a short trace (mc-request-trace.txt) and SLO snapshot. Recommend option 1 + 2 while we patch the underlying kernel eviction/rebalancing bug.

-Neha
SRE

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example, sean_gallagher@redwood.example
Date: 2026-12-02T10:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — reserved pool underperforming

Looping in leadership for an emergency decision. Proposed immediate exec ask: approve a one-time emergency capacity burst for Finly (cost charged to Redwood's emergency tolerance fund for customer retention) to reduce impact while SREs complete rebalancing.

Rationale: Finly is a strategic mid-market account with an active expansion deal (DL-2025-774). The customer impact is severe during their business hours; routing to hosted could reduce latency but increases our per-token exposure and creates potential quality complaints.

Ask for execs:
- Yes/No on emergency +15% capacity for 3 hours (we estimate this will clear backlog and reduce 504s immediately).
- Approval to issue a one-off minor account credit if we miss SLA for today's peak window (amount TBD).

I've drafted a 15‑minute ops+exec sync at 11:00 PT to make the call. Laura — can you confirm Finly will accept hosted fallback if we propose that?

-Vivek
Head of Customer Reliability

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.example
To: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@finly.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example
Date: 2026-12-03T16:45:00Z
Subject: Incident update and next steps — Finly reserved pool recovery

Tom — follow-up and summary from our mitigation window: 

What happened: a combination of a transient burst from a customer RL batch job and a kernel eviction bug on two nodes caused queue buildup and higher latencies in your reserved pool.

What we did (timeline):
- 2026-12-02 08:40 PT: SRE escalated; triggered emergency +15% capacity burst and shifted 25% of traffic to a hosted-compatible variant to immediately reduce error surface.
- 2026-12-02 09:20 PT: backlog drained; error rate returned to <0.2% for the remainder of the day.
- 2026-12-03 06:00 PT: permanent kernel patch deployed to affected nodes and rebalancing completed.

Customer-visible outcomes: 504s peaked during the window but were contained after mitigation. We captured traces and have a remediation patch in place. We've attached the incident artifacts and SLO snapshots so your ops team can validate.

Next steps: 
- We recommend a 30-day monitoring window with daily SLO snaps and a follow-up postmortem shared by 2026-12-07.
- If you prefer, we will formalize a minor account credit for today's impact; Laura will follow up on compensation language.
- Ops: share any additional traces or repro steps you see — we'll prioritize.

Thanks for your patience; we know this impacted a critical window. We'll keep the channel open and will set up a short readout with your platform engineers.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mc-request-trace.txt, slo-snapshot-20261202.png
